- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75%), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–3% downward bias to forecast.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event balance is net bearish, model often fails to adjust downward; apply mean reversion to last 5–7 days’ average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just historical mean.  
- If multiple consecutive auctions (e.g., CAP3 EU) occur, model overreacts to supply; reduce forecast sensitivity to supply net by 15–20% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
